claims.statement: Wihwin is a malevolent water spirit of Central America, associated especially with the Miskito tribe.
claims.statement_id: Wihwin adalah roh air jahat dari Amerika Tengah yang terutama dikaitkan dengan suku Miskito.
claims.quote: Wihwin is the name given to a malevolent water spirit of Central America, particularly associated with the Miskito tribe.

claims.statement: Similar creatures include the kelpie in Scotland, the Scandinavian bäckahäst and the Australian bunyip.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk mitologi serupa antara lain kelpie di Skotlandia, bäckahäst di Skandinavia, dan bunyip di Australia.
claims.quote: Similar mythological creatures around the world include the kelpie in Scotland, the Scandinavian bäckahäst and the Australian bunyip.

claims.statement: Though normally sea-dwelling, it roams mountain ridges in the summer months.
claims.statement_id: Meski biasanya tinggal di laut, ia berkeliaran di punggung-punggung gunung pada musim panas.
claims.quote: Although normally a sea-dwelling demon, it prowls through mountain ridges during the summer months.

claims.statement: The horse-shaped monster has jaws of horrid teeth with which it devours humans and other prey on its nocturnal hunts.
claims.statement_id: Monster berbentuk kuda ini memiliki rahang bergigi mengerikan yang dipakainya untuk memangsa manusia dan mangsa lain dalam perburuan malamnya.
claims.quote: The horse-shaped monster has "jaws fenced round with horrid teeth", which it uses to consume humans and other prey it finds on its nocturnal hunts.

claims.statement: Xicalancatl (also Xicallancatl or Xicalcoatl) is one of the six giant sons of Mixcoatl and Tlaltecuhtli who populated the Earth after the Great Flood in the Fifth Sun of Aztec mythology.
claims.statement_id: Xicalancatl (juga Xicallancatl atau Xicalcoatl) adalah salah satu dari enam raksasa putra Mixcoatl dan Tlaltecuhtli yang menghuni Bumi setelah Air Bah pada masa Matahari Kelima dalam mitologi Aztek.
claims.quote: Xicalancatl, Xicallancatl or Xicalcoatl (From Nahuatl, 'Teacup Serpent') is one of the six giants sons of Mixcoatl and Tlaltecuhtli that populated the Earth after the Great Flood during the Fifth Sun in Aztec Mythology.

claims.statement: He was the fourth son, who settled on the coasts of the Gulf of Mexico in the region called Xicallanco.
claims.statement_id: Ia putra keempat yang menetap di pesisir Teluk Meksiko, di wilayah bernama Xicallanco.
claims.quote: The fourth son who settled on the coasts of the Gulf of Mexico, in the region called Xicallanco

claims.statement: The six brothers dwell on earth and are the trunk of various races.
claims.statement_id: Keenam bersaudara itu tinggal di bumi dan menjadi leluhur berbagai bangsa.
claims.quote: the six brothers on earth dwell and are the trunk of various races

claims.statement: Adjassou-Linguetor is a loa with protruding eyes and a bad temper in Haitian Vodou.
claims.statement_id: Adjassou-Linguetor adalah loa bermata menonjol dan bertemperamen buruk dalam Vodou Haiti.
claims.quote: Adjassou-Linguetor is a loa with protruding eyes and a bad temper in Haitian Vodou.

claims.statement: In Haitian Vodou, she governs spring water.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Vodou Haiti, ia menguasai air mata air.
claims.quote: in Haitian Vodou. She governs spring water.

claims.statement: In the table of Plaisance Vodun deities, Adjassou-Linguetor is listed with names given as equivalents: Adja or Adja Bosu (Courlander), Agasu (Herskovits), or Aguasu (Dorsainvil).
claims.statement_id: Dalam daftar dewa Vodun di Plaisance, Adjassou-Linguetor dicatat bersama nama-nama yang disamakan dengannya: Adja atau Adja Bosu (Courlander), Agasu (Herskovits), atau Aguasu (Dorsainvil).
claims.quote: PLAISANCE VopuN Detties* Loa Informants Adjassou-Linguetor A.G. Ar. Adja or Adja Bosu, Courlander, op. cit., 30; or Agasu, Herskovits (1), 267; or Aguasu, Dor- sainvil, op. cit., 174

claims.statement: In the same article's table, the row for Adjasou records protruding eyes, no special robe, always in a bad humor, and an abode under the mombin tree near a spring.
claims.statement_id: Dalam tabel yang sama, baris Adjasou mencatat mata menonjol, tanpa jubah khusus, selalu bersuasana hati buruk, dan berdiam di bawah pohon mombin dekat mata air.
claims.quote: Adjasou Protruding eyes. No special robe. Under the mom- ... Always in a bad bin tree near a ... humor. spring.

claims.statement: The table's footnote says it is a combined list of Joas (loas) given by nine non-literate informants.
claims.statement_id: Catatan tabel itu menyebut daftar dewa tersebut merupakan gabungan nama Joa (loa) yang diberikan sembilan informan yang tidak melek huruf.
claims.quote: This is a combined list of Joas given by nine non-literate informants

claims.statement: According to one view near Plaisance, the Saints and the Joas (loas) are intermediaries between God, creator of man and master of the universe, and man.
claims.statement_id: Menurut salah satu pandangan di sekitar Plaisance, para Santo dan Joa (loa) adalah perantara antara Tuhan, pencipta manusia dan penguasa semesta, dan manusia.
claims.quote: The Saints and the Joas are intermediaries between God, the creator of man and the master of the Universe, and man.

claims.statement: The Caballo Marino Chilote ("Chilote sea horse") is an aquatic creature of Chilote mythology in Chile that resembles the hippocampus.
claims.statement_id: Caballo Marino Chilote ("kuda laut Chilote") adalah makhluk air dalam mitologi Chilote di Chile yang agak mirip hippocampus.
claims.quote: The Caballo Marino Chilote (chilote sea horse) is an aquatic creature of the Chilote mythology of Chile, that bears some resemblance to the hippocampus.

claims.statement: Legend says it is invisible and can only be seen by those with magical powers.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda, makhluk ini tak kasatmata dan hanya dapat dilihat oleh orang berkekuatan gaib.
claims.quote: Legend says that the "Caballo marino chilote" is an invisible creature, which could only be seen by those with magical powers.

claims.statement: It looks like a normal horse but with a longer snout, golden mane, four fin-like paws and a long fish-like tail.
claims.statement_id: Wujudnya seperti kuda biasa, tetapi bermoncong lebih panjang, bersurai emas, berkaki empat berbentuk sirip, dan berekor panjang seperti ekor ikan.
claims.quote: The creature would look like a normal horse, but would have the longer snout, golden mane, four paws in the form of fins, and a long tail, similar to the tail of a fish.

claims.statement: They exist in various sizes, from dwarfs to giants.
claims.statement_id: Ukurannya beragam, dari kerdil hingga raksasa.
claims.quote: They can exist in various sizes, from dwarfs to giants.

claims.statement: The Brujo Chilote (a sorcerer) rides it to reach the Caleuche ghost ship.
claims.statement_id: Brujo Chilote (sejenis penyihir) memakainya sebagai tunggangan untuk mencapai kapal hantu Caleuche.
claims.quote: The Brujo Chilote (a type of sorcerer or warlock) would use a "Caballo marino chilote" as transportation to get to the Caleuche ghost ship.

claims.statement: According to Quintana, the rules of witchcraft require the brujos to join the Caleuche's crew only by arriving on the back of the Caballo Marino.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Quintana, aturan ilmu sihir mengharuskan para brujo hanya bergabung sebagai awak Caleuche dengan datang di punggung Caballo Marino.
claims.quote: la reglamentación de la brujería, por razones de ignoro, les ordena que sólo puedan integrarse como tripulantes del Caleuche, llegando sobre el lomo del Caballo Marino.

claims.statement: When the brujo needs this mount he goes to the sea shore a few minutes before midnight and whistles four special whistles; at the last whistle the Caballo Marino appears panting.
claims.statement_id: Ketika membutuhkan tunggangan itu, sang brujo mendekati tepi laut beberapa menit sebelum tengah malam dan bersiul empat kali; begitu siulan terakhir terdengar, Caballo Marino muncul terengah-engah.
claims.quote: se acerca a las orillas del mar, pocos minutos antes de la medianoche y desde ese lugar, lanza cuatro silbidos especiales. Apenas escuchando el último silbido, aparece jadeante el Caballo Marino

claims.statement: Sea horses, visible only to members of the witchcraft society, live in large numbers in the sea and are born in the domains of the Millalobo, in the Pacific Ocean off the western coast of the Island of Chiloé.
claims.statement_id: Caballo marino hanya terlihat oleh anggota perkumpulan sihir, hidup dalam jumlah besar di laut, dan lahir di wilayah kekuasaan Millalobo di Samudra Pasifik, di depan pesisir barat Pulau Chiloé.
claims.quote: Los caballos marinos, sólo visibles por los miembros de la brujería, habitan en gran cantidad en el mar, nacen en los dominios del Millalobo, en el océano pacífico, frente a la costa occidental de la Isla de Chiloé.

claims.statement: According to Quintana, it feeds on seaweed, especially luche and cochayuyo, which give it a dark yellowish-green colour.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Quintana, caballo marino makan rumput laut, terutama luche dan cochayuyo, yang memberinya warna hijau kekuningan gelap.
claims.quote: Se alimenta de algas marinas, especialmente de luche y cochayuyo que les transmiten su color verdoso amarillento obscuro.

claims.statement: Each brujo has one or more; there are small ones for individual service and larger ones for collective use, and the largest can carry a full board of thirteen brujos.
claims.statement_id: Setiap brujo memiliki satu kuda laut atau lebih; ada yang kecil untuk satu penunggang dan yang lebih besar untuk dipakai bersama, dan yang terbesar dapat mengangkut satu pengurus lengkap beranggotakan tiga belas brujo.
claims.quote: Cada brujo dispone de uno o más caballos. Los hay pequeños, para servicio individual y de mayor tamaño, para uso colectivo; los más grandes pueden transportar una directiva completa de brujos, integrada por trece miembros.

claims.statement: The brujos choose the sea horses they like and place their mark on them, after which the animal remains permanently at their service.
claims.statement_id: Para brujo memilih kuda laut yang mereka sukai dan menandainya; sejak itu hewan itu tetap melayani mereka.
claims.quote: los brujos elijen los caballos de su agrado y les colocan su marca, acto en el cual, al animal queda permanentemente a su servicio.

claims.statement: According to Quintana, sea horses live only four years and, once dead, their bodies turn into a kind of gelatin that quickly dissolves in the brackish sea water.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Quintana, caballo marino hanya hidup empat tahun, dan begitu mati tubuhnya berubah menjadi semacam gelatin yang cepat larut dalam air laut.
claims.quote: Los caballos marinos viven sólo cautro años y tan pronto mueren, sus cuerpos se transforman en una especie de gelatina, que rápidamente se disuelve en las aguas salobres del mar

claims.statement: Quintana considers the origin of the myth hard to determine and suggests it may be a mistranslation of the myth's name into Spanish, so that it would not correspond exactly to the horse brought by the Spaniards (which did not exist in Chiloé) but to another kind of mount.
claims.statement_id: Quintana menilai asal-usul mitos ini sulit ditentukan dan menduga mungkin terjadi salah terjemah nama mitos ke bahasa Spanyol, sehingga ia tidak persis berarti kuda yang dibawa orang Spanyol (yang tidak ada di Chiloé), melainkan jenis tunggangan lain.
claims.quote: Los orígenes de este mito, son difíciles de determinar, podría tratarse de una mala traducción del nombre del mito al castellano y por lo tanto, no correspondería exactamente al caballo traído por los españoles y que no existía en Chiloé, sino a otro tipo de cabalgadura.

claims.statement: Quintana also suggests the idea may have arisen from watching the fin of a marine animal, which from a distance and with a little imagination looks as if it carries a rider on its back.
claims.statement_id: Quintana juga mengemukakan bahwa gagasan ini mungkin lahir dari pemandangan sirip hewan laut yang dari kejauhan, dengan sedikit imajinasi, tampak membawa penunggang di punggungnya.
claims.quote: O la idea pudo haber nacido, al contemplar la aleta de un animal marino, que a la distancia y con un poco de imaginación, simula llevar a un jinete en el lomo

claims.statement: The Museo de Ancud's collection note describes the Caballo Marino as a horse that lives in the sea and belongs to the brujos, gigantic and of horrendous appearance, which more than thirteen people can ride.
claims.statement_id: Dalam keterangan koleksi Museo de Ancud, Caballo Marino digambarkan sebagai kuda yang hidup di laut dan milik para brujo, raksasa dan berpenampilan mengerikan, dengan lebih dari tiga belas orang dapat menungganginya.
claims.quote: Caballo que vive en el mar y pertenece a los brujos. Es gigantesco y de apariencia horrenda. En él pueden montar más de trece personas.

claims.statement: The Museo de Ancud quotes Oreste Plath, who calls the Caballo Marino the personification of the sea waves, always appearing with foam from its mouth and governable only with reins of sargassum.
claims.statement_id: Museo de Ancud mengutip Oreste Plath yang menyebut Caballo Marino sebagai personifikasi ombak laut yang selalu muncul menyemburkan buih dari mulutnya, dan hanya dapat dikendalikan dengan tali kekang dari sargazo.
claims.quote: El Caballo Marino es la personificación de las olas del mar, y siempre aparece arrojando espuma por la boca. No se le puede gobernar sino con riendas de sargazo

claims.statement: The Museo de Ancud records figures of mythological beings made of plant fibre in 1977 by craftspeople of Isla Llingua (commune of Quinchao); the figures include the Caballo Marino.
claims.statement_id: Museo de Ancud mencatat figur makhluk mitologi dari serat tumbuhan yang dibuat pada 1977 oleh para perajin Isla Llingua (komune Quinchao), dan figur-figur itu mencakup Caballo Marino.
claims.quote: Figuras de seres mitológicos confeccionadas con fibra vegetal, elaboradas en 1977 por artesanas y artesanos de Isla Llingua (comuna de Quinchao).

claims.statement: The museum collection lists a Caballo Marino figure in plant fibre, 22 x 30 cm, by Deifilia Mansilla Miranda, in the Cestería de Chiloé collection.
claims.statement_id: Koleksi museum mencantumkan sebuah figur Caballo Marino dari serat tumbuhan berukuran 22 x 30 cm karya Deifilia Mansilla Miranda, dalam koleksi Cestería de Chiloé.
claims.quote: Deifilia Mansilla Miranda. Caballo Marino. Fibra vegetal. 22 x 30 cm. Cestería de Chiloé. En exhibición. Nº inventario 1094.

claims.statement: The Caboclo de Agua is a mythological being of northeastern Brazil said to live at the bottom of the São Francisco River in a golden grotto, frightening fishermen and boatmen.
claims.statement_id: Caboclo de Agua adalah makhluk mitologi dari timur laut Brasil yang konon tinggal di dasar Sungai São Francisco dalam gua emas dan menakut-nakuti nelayan serta pelaut.
claims.quote: El Caboclo de Agua es un ser mitológico del nordeste de Brasil que supuestamente habita en el fondo de las aguas del Río São Francisco en una gruta de oro y se dedica a asustar a pescadores y navegantes.

claims.statement: Locals describe it as a giant, muscular being with bronze skin and a single huge eye.
claims.statement_id: Penduduk setempat menggambarkannya sebagai makhluk raksasa berotot, berkulit perunggu, dengan satu mata besar di kepala.
claims.quote: Los nativos lo describen como un ser gigante y musculoso, con piel de color bronce y un único ojo gigante en la cabeza.

claims.statement: Its heart is very hard and impenetrable to bullets.
claims.statement_id: Jantungnya sangat keras dan tak tembus peluru.
claims.quote: Tiene un corazón muy duro impenetrable a las balas.

claims.statement: It can also appear as other animals, such as horses.
claims.statement_id: Ia juga dapat muncul dalam wujud hewan lain, seperti kuda.
claims.quote: También puede aparecer bajo la apariencia de otros animales, como caballos.

claims.statement: If it dislikes a fisherman it drives fish from his nets; if it likes him, it fills them.
claims.statement_id: Jika tidak menyukai seorang nelayan, ia mengusir ikan dari jaringnya; jika menyukainya, ia membuat jaringnya penuh.
claims.quote: Cuando no le cae bien un pescador, ahuyenta a la pesca de las redes. Cuando le cae bien algún hombre, logra que se le llenen las redes.

claims.statement: It often chases boats (embarcaciones) to make them capsize (volcar).
claims.statement_id: Ia sering mengejar perahu (embarcaciones) untuk membuatnya terbalik (volcar).
claims.quote: A menudo persigue a las embarcaciones para hacerlas volcar.

claims.statement: To ward it off, river fishermen put monstrous figures called "carrancas" on their bows.
claims.statement_id: Untuk mengusirnya, nelayan memasang figur seram bernama "carrancas" di haluan perahu.
claims.quote: Para ahuyentarlo, los pescadores del río construyen en la proa de sus barcos, figuras monstruosas llamadas "carrancas".

claims.statement: They also paint a star on the bottom of the boat, believed to scare supernatural beings.
claims.statement_id: Mereka juga melukis bintang di dasar perahu karena dipercaya menakuti makhluk gaib.
claims.quote: También pintan una estrella en el fondo de la barca pues se cree que espanta a los seres sobrenaturales.

claims.statement: According to Cascudo, the Caboclo-d'Água is a fantastic creature that lives in the São Francisco River and holds dominion over the waters and the fish.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Cascudo, Caboclo-d'Água adalah makhluk fantastis yang hidup di Sungai São Francisco dan berkuasa atas air serta ikan.
claims.quote: Criatura fantástica que vive no rio São Francisco, tendo o do- mínio sobre as águas e os peixes.

claims.statement: According to Cascudo, it favours its friends and compadres but fiercely pursues the fishermen and riverbank dwellers it dislikes, among other things by overturning canoes.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Cascudo, ia berpihak pada para sahabat dan kompadrenya, tetapi memburu dengan ganas para nelayan dan penghuni tepi sungai yang tidak disukainya, antara lain dengan membalikkan kano.
claims.quote: compadres do caboclo-d'água, e persegue ferozmente aos pescadores e barranqueiros, com que antipatiza, virando canoas,

claims.statement: Cascudo records other names of the Caboclo-d'água: Bicho-d'água, Rolão, Romão and Romãozinho.
claims.statement_id: Cascudo mencatat nama lain Caboclo-d'água: Bicho-d'água, Rolão, Romão, dan Romãozinho.
claims.quote: O Caboclo-d'água também é chamado Bicho-d'água, Rolão, Romão (ver Romãozinho), Romãozinho,

claims.statement: In a passage quoted by Cascudo, its body is monstrous, with the proportions of an enormous giant.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kutipan yang dimuat Cascudo, tubuhnya mengerikan dengan proporsi raksasa yang luar biasa.
claims.quote: Seu corpo é monstruoso, com as proporções de um gigante descomu- nal.

claims.statement: In a passage quoted by Cascudo, the type reported by the most testimonies is short, thick, muscular, copper-coloured, quick in movement and always ill-tempered.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kutipan yang dimuat Cascudo, tipe yang paling banyak dilaporkan adalah pendek, tebal, berotot, berwarna tembaga, gesit, dan selalu pemarah.
claims.quote: O tipo do caboclo- -d'água que recolhe maior número de depoimentos é o seguinte: baixo, gros- so, musculoso, cor de cobre, rápido nos movimentos e sempre enfezado.

claims.statement: According to Cascudo, through a convergence with the myth of the Curupira-Caapora, the boatmen of the São Francisco offer tobacco to the Caboclo-d'água.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Cascudo, karena pertemuan dengan mitos Curupira-Caapora, para pengayuh perahu di São Francisco mempersembahkan tembakau kepada Caboclo-d'água.
claims.quote: Por uma convergência do mito do Curupira-Caapora, os barqueiros do São Francisco oferecem fumo ao cabo- clo-d'água.

claims.statement: In a passage quoted by Cascudo, a traveller going far alone and facing fearsome crossings sticks his knife in the bottom of the canoe, and the monster, guessing this, does not attack the passer-by at all.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kutipan yang dimuat Cascudo, orang yang bepergian jauh sendirian dan harus menempuh penyeberangan menakutkan menancapkan pisaunya di dasar kano, dan monster itu, yang menduganya, sama sekali tidak menyerang.
claims.quote: quem via- ja para longe, sozinho, e tem de arros- tar temerosas travessias, finca sua faca no fundo da canoa, e o monstro, que isto adivinha, de forma alguma acomete o transeunte

claims.statement: The Camahueto is a legendary bull of Chilote mythology.
claims.statement_id: Camahueto adalah banteng legendaris dalam mitologi Chilote.
claims.quote: The Camahueto is a legendary bull found in Chilote mythology.

claims.statement: From the Chiloé Archipelago, it was said to have a single horn on its forehead like a unicorn's.
claims.statement_id: Berasal dari Kepulauan Chiloé, banteng ini konon bertanduk tunggal di dahi seperti unicorn.
claims.quote: Originating in the Chiloé Archipelago, the bull was said to have a single horn on its forehead, similar to a unicorn's.

claims.statement: It is said to grow in rivers and move to the ocean when fully grown.
claims.statement_id: Camahueto konon tumbuh di sungai dan pindah ke laut setelah dewasa.
claims.quote: The Camahueto is said to grow within rivers, moving to the ocean when they are fully grown.

claims.statement: Various versions say it eats humans, controls time and creates rain or thunder at will.
claims.statement_id: Menurut berbagai versi, ia memangsa manusia, mengendalikan waktu, dan menciptakan hujan atau petir sesukanya.
claims.quote: it is variously said to eat humans, control time and create rain or thunder at will.

claims.statement: Legends tell of people dragged into the sea for crossing its path or nearing its resting place.
claims.statement_id: Legenda menceritakan orang yang ditarik ke dasar laut karena menghalangi jalannya atau mendekati tempat istirahatnya.
claims.quote: Legends tell of humans being dragged into the depths of the sea by the Camahueto when they cross its path, or approach its resting place.

claims.statement: The only way to be rid of it is to call a machi, who can lead it back to sea with a kelp lasso.
claims.statement_id: Satu-satunya cara mengusirnya adalah meminta bantuan machi yang dapat menggiringnya kembali ke laut dengan laso dari rumput laut.
claims.quote: the only way to rid yourself of a Camahueto is to call for the aid of a machi, or witch, who can lead the animal back to sea using a lasso made of kelp.

claims.statement: According to Chiloé Mitológico, the Camahueto looks like a green calf with a single small horn on its forehead, like its Greek counterpart the Unicorn.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Chiloé Mitológico, Camahueto berwujud anak sapi berwarna hijau dengan satu tanduk kecil di dahi, mirip unicorn Yunani.
claims.quote: tiene el aspecto de un ternero, de color verde, con un solo cuerno pequeño en la frente; a semejanza de su congénere griego el Unicornio.

claims.statement: The Camahueto is born from the depths of the earth, on top of a hill near the sea.
claims.statement_id: Camahueto lahir dari kedalaman bumi, di puncak sebuah bukit dekat laut.
claims.quote: Nace desde las profundidades de la tierra, en lo alto de un cerro vecino al mar.

claims.statement: As soon as a machi sees the Camahueto, he skilfully catches it with a lasso made of "boqui", tears off its horn ("cacho") and lets it go on its way to the sea.
claims.statement_id: Begitu melihat Camahueto, seorang machi menangkapnya dengan laso dari "boqui", mencabut tanduknya ("cacho"), lalu melepasnya agar melanjutkan perjalanan ke laut.
claims.quote: En cuanto divisa al Camahueto, lo coge hábilmente, con un lazo hecho de «boqui», y después de arrancarle su «cacho», lo suelta para que siga su camino hacia el mar.

claims.statement: The machis plant small pieces of the horn on other hills, and after twenty-five years other camahuetos are born.
claims.statement_id: Para machi menanam potongan kecil tanduk itu di bukit lain, dan setelah dua puluh lima tahun lahirlah camahueto lain.
claims.quote: Los machis, ciembran pequños trozos de él, en otros cerros y transcurridos veinticinco años, nacen otros camahuetos

claims.statement: Scrapings of the horn are described as the most effective of all the medicines in the early Chilote pharmacopoeia, for curing every kind of illness.
claims.statement_id: Kerokan tanduk itu disebut sebagai obat paling manjur di antara semua obat dalam farmakope Chiloé kuno untuk menyembuhkan segala penyakit.
claims.quote: Las mencionadas raspaduras, constituyen el más eficaz de todos los medicamentos, que consigna la primitiva farmacopea chilota, para curar todo tipo de enfermedades.

claims.statement: In the site author's interpretation, this imaginary animal was used to explain the frequent, apparently spontaneous landslides caused by water accumulating underground.
claims.statement_id: Menurut penafsiran penulis situs ini, hewan imajiner ini dipakai untuk menjelaskan longsor tanah yang sering terjadi dan tampak spontan, akibat air yang menumpuk di bawah tanah.
claims.quote: se recurrió a este animal imaginario, para explicar los frecuentes y aparentemente espontáneos derrumbes de tierra, que ocasionan las aguas que se van acumulando bajo tierra

claims.statement: The site author adds that the Camahueto represents strength, fertility and abundance.
claims.statement_id: Penulis situs ini menambahkan bahwa Camahueto melambangkan kekuatan, kesuburan, dan kelimpahan.
claims.quote: Además representa la fuerza, la fecundidad y la abundancia.

claims.statement: Little is known of the Camahueto's aquatic life, so it is classed among the land myths; it is said to return to the sea because it belongs there and will live its true existence there.
claims.statement_id: Kehidupan akuatik Camahueto hampir tidak diketahui sehingga ia digolongkan sebagai mitos darat; konon ia kembali ke laut karena laut adalah miliknya dan di sanalah ia menjalani keberadaan sejatinya.
claims.quote: De la vida acuática el camahueto, se sabe muy poco y por tal motivo lo incluimos entre los mitos terrestres; se dice que regresa al mar, porque a él pertenece y allí realizará su verdadera existencia.

claims.statement: According to this source, its stay on land is only a form of revenge left behind by the water spirit Coicoi-vilu on his retreat, to continue his destructive work on land.
claims.statement_id: Menurut sumber ini, keberadaannya di darat hanyalah bentuk pembalasan yang ditinggalkan roh air Coicoi-vilu saat mundur, untuk melanjutkan karya perusaknya di darat.
claims.quote: Y que su estadía en la tierra, sólo representa una forma de venganza, que dejó en su retirada, el espíritu de las aguas, Coicoi-vilu, para continuar su obra destructora en la tierra.

claims.statement: Chasca, also called "la virgen del agua" (the virgin of the water), is a character of Salvadoran folklore.
claims.statement_id: Chasca, juga disebut "la virgen del agua" (perawan air), adalah tokoh dalam cerita rakyat El Salvador.
claims.quote: Chasca, also known as "la virgen del agua" (The virgin of the water), is the name of a fictional character in Salvadoran folklore.

claims.statement: According to oral tradition, Pachacutec of the barra de Santiago arranged for his daughter Chasca to marry a zutuhil prince.
claims.statement_id: Menurut tradisi lisan, Pachacutec di barra de Santiago menjodohkan putrinya, Chasca, dengan pangeran suku zutuhil.
claims.quote: According to oral tradition, in the barra de Santiago lived a man named Pachacutec, who arranged a marriage between his daughter, Chasca, and a prince of the zutuhil tribe.

claims.statement: But Chasca already loved a young fisher named Acayatl.
claims.statement_id: Namun Chasca telah mencintai nelayan muda bernama Acayatl.
claims.quote: Chasca, however, was already in love with a young fisher named Acayatl.

claims.statement: Acayatl's assassin was sent by Pachacutec.
claims.statement_id: Pembunuh Acayatl diutus oleh Pachacutec.
claims.quote: The assassin was sent by Pachacutec.

claims.statement: Chasca tied a rock around her waist and threw herself into the water.
claims.statement_id: Chasca mengikat batu di pinggangnya dan menceburkan diri ke air.
claims.quote: She tied a rock around her waist and threw herself into the water.

claims.statement: On the next full-moon night, her spirit first appeared in a white canoe beside Acayatl.
claims.statement_id: Pada malam bulan purnama berikutnya, roh Chasca muncul untuk pertama kali dalam kano putih di samping Acayatl.
claims.quote: The following night of a full moon, the spirit of Chasca appeared for the first time in a white canoe next to Acayatl

claims.statement: On full-moon nights, fishermen do not go fishing, out of respect for the virgin of the water and her lover.
claims.statement_id: Saat bulan purnama, para nelayan tidak melaut untuk menghormati dan tidak mengganggu perawan air dan kekasihnya.
claims.quote: Whenever the fishermen notice a full moon, they do not go out to fish because they wish to respect and not disturb the virgin of the water and her lover

claims.statement: In return, the pair bless the fishermen with bountiful fish.
claims.statement_id: Sebagai balasan, keduanya memberkati nelayan dengan tangkapan melimpah.
claims.quote: who in return for that respect, bless the fishermen with bountiful fish.

claims.statement: According to El Salvador's Ministry of Culture, the Ballet Folklórico Nacional brings to life a show based on the narration collected by the author Miguel Ángel Espino in his book "Mitología de Cuscatlán".
claims.statement_id: Menurut Kementerian Kebudayaan El Salvador, Ballet Folklórico Nacional menghidupkan pertunjukan yang berdasar pada kisah yang dihimpun penulis Miguel Ángel Espino dalam bukunya "Mitología de Cuscatlán".
claims.quote: el Ballet Folklórico Nacional da vida al espectáculo basado en la narración que recoje el autor Miguel Ángel Espino en su libro “Mitología de Cuscatlán”

claims.statement: The show "Chasca, la virgen del agua", with which the Ballet Folklórico Nacional celebrates its 46 years of history, was performed again at the Teatro Nacional de San Salvador at the public's request.
claims.statement_id: Pertunjukan "Chasca, la virgen del agua", yang dengannya Ballet Folklórico Nacional merayakan 46 tahun perjalanannya, dipentaskan kembali di Teatro Nacional de San Salvador atas permintaan publik.
claims.quote: El exitoso espectáculo con el que el Ballet Folklórico Nacional celebra sus 46 años de trayectoria, “Chasca, la virgen del agua”, se presentó nuevamente en el Teatro Nacional de San Salvador, a petición del público.

claims.statement: That year the ballet staged the loyal and eternal love between Chasca and the young fisherman, written here as Acayet.
claims.statement_id: Tahun itu ballet tersebut mementaskan cinta setia dan abadi antara Chasca dan nelayan muda yang di sumber ini ditulis Acayet.
claims.quote: un objetivo para el que este año lleva a escena el amor leal y eterno entre Chasca y el jóven pescador Acayet

claims.statement: The Ministry of Culture's news item about the show was published on 17 June 2023.
claims.statement_id: Berita Kementerian Kebudayaan tentang pertunjukan ini diterbitkan pada 17 Juni 2023.
claims.quote: Publicado el 17-06-2023. Etiquetas: 46.° Aniversario, Ballet Folklórico Nacional

claims.statement: The besta-fera is a mythical being of Portuguese and Brazilian folklore.
claims.statement_id: Besta-fera adalah makhluk mitos dalam cerita rakyat Portugal dan Brasil.
claims.quote: A besta-fera é um ser mítico do folclore português e brasileiro.

claims.statement: It is a creature of indefinite features that eats people and has a frightening roar.
claims.statement_id: Wujudnya tidak jelas; ia memakan manusia dan raungannya menakutkan.
claims.quote: É uma criatura de traços indefinidos comedora de gente e que tem um rugido assustador.

claims.statement: The myth was presumably brought to Brazil by Portuguese colonists.
claims.statement_id: Mitos hewan fantastis ini diduga dibawa ke Brasil oleh kolonis Portugis.
claims.quote: O mito deste animal fantástico terá sido levado para o Brasil pelos colonizadores portugueses.

claims.statement: The besta-fera is also said to be a Brazilian version of the centaur.
claims.statement_id: Besta-fera juga disebut versi Brasil dari centaur.
claims.quote: Também se diz que a besta-fera é uma versão brasileira do centauro

claims.statement: It is believed to be the Devil himself, leaving Hell on full-moon nights to put the "mark of the beast" on people.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda, ia adalah Iblis sendiri yang keluar dari Neraka pada malam bulan purnama untuk memberi "tanda binatang" pada manusia.
claims.quote: acredita-se que ele é o próprio Diabo, que sai do Inferno em noites de lua cheia para colocar o "sinal da besta" nas pessoas

claims.statement: The besta-fera has the body of a horse and a human torso.
claims.statement_id: Besta-fera bertubuh kuda dan berbadan atas manusia.
claims.quote: A besta-fera tem o corpo de cavalo e o dorso humano.

claims.statement: Tradition says whoever sees its face goes mad for several days but then recovers.
claims.statement_id: Orang yang melihat wajahnya konon menjadi gila beberapa hari, lalu pulih.
claims.quote: A tradição diz que quando uma pessoa vê o seu rosto, ela enlouquece por vários dias, mas se recupera depois.

claims.statement: Besta-fera is a centaur-like creature thought to be the Devil; the name roughly means "Feral Beast" or "Bestial Beast".
claims.statement_id: Besta-fera adalah makhluk mirip centaur yang dianggap Iblis; namanya kira-kira berarti "binatang buas".
claims.quote: Besta-fera – a centaur-like creature, thought to be the Devil. The name can be roughly translated as "Feral Beast" or "Bestial Beast".

claims.statement: The Capelobo is a part-animal creature of Brazilian mythology with the snout of a pig, dog or giant anteater, depending on region, told in Pará or Maranhão.
claims.statement_id: Capelobo adalah makhluk setengah hewan dalam mitologi Brasil dengan moncong babi, anjing, atau trenggiling raksasa tergantung daerahnya, diceritakan di Pará atau Maranhão.
claims.quote: The Capelobo is a therianthropic creature from Brazilian mythology, with an elongated snout of a pig, dog, or giant anteater, depending on region, as the legend is locally told in the states of Pará or Maranhão.

claims.statement: It is feared as a man-eater, specifically a blood-sucker and brain-eater.
claims.statement_id: Ia ditakuti sebagai pemangsa manusia, khususnya pengisap darah dan pemakan otak.
claims.quote: It is feared as a man-eater, more specifically a blood-sucker and brain-eater.

claims.statement: The name combines Guarani capê ("crooked" or "lame") and Portuguese lobo ("wolf").
claims.statement_id: Nama Capelobo menggabungkan kata Guarani capê ("pincang" atau "bengkok") dan kata Portugis lobo ("serigala").
claims.quote: The name Capelobo is a fusion of Guarani capê meaning "broken boned", "crooked", "crook-legged", or "lame" and the Portuguese word lobo ... meaning wolf.

claims.statement: In the popular Xingu River basin version, the Capelobo has an animal form and a humanoid form.
claims.statement_id: Dalam versi populer di lembah Sungai Xingu, Pará, Capelobo punya dua wujud: hewan dan mirip manusia.
claims.quote: In the version which is widely popular in the Xingu River basin, Pará, the Capelobo has two forms, an animal form and a humanoid form.

claims.statement: In animal form it resembles a long, black-haired tapir with a dog or pig snout.
claims.statement_id: Dalam wujud hewan, ia mirip tapir berbulu hitam panjang bermoncong anjing atau babi.
claims.quote: In its animal form, it resembles a long, black haired and dog- or pig-snouted tapir

claims.statement: The Maranhão version is called Cupelobo and reputedly has a giant anteater snout.
claims.statement_id: Versi Maranhão disebut Cupelobo dan konon bermoncong trenggiling raksasa.
claims.quote: The version in Maranhão (apparently surviving in the forests of the Pindaré River basin if nowhere else) is called Cupelobo (cupélobo) and reputed to have the snout of a giant anteater.

claims.statement: The Capelobo is described as a blood-sucker and likened to the werewolf Lobisomem, or considered a sub-variant of it.
claims.statement_id: Capelobo digambarkan sebagai pengisap darah dan disamakan dengan manusia serigala Lobisomem, atau dianggap variannya.
claims.quote: The Capelobo is described as a hematophage (blood-sucker) and likened to the werewolf Lobisomem (or considered a sub-variant thereof).

claims.statement: The only way to defeat it is to shoot it in the navel, which is covered in long fur.
claims.statement_id: Satu-satunya cara mengalahkannya adalah menembak pusarnya yang tertutup bulu panjang.
claims.quote: The only way to defeat it is by shooting it in the navel, which is covered in long strands of fur

claims.statement: The Capelobo screams a lot to announce itself, like the Mapinguari and the Pé de Garrafa.
claims.statement_id: Capelobo banyak berteriak untuk menandai kehadirannya, seperti Mapinguari dan Pé de Garrafa.
claims.quote: The Capelobo does a lot of screaming to announce its presence, like the Mapinguari and the Pé de Garrafa.

claims.statement: In Cascudo's Dicionário do Folclore Brasileiro, the Capelobo or Cupelobo is a fantastic animal with a human body and the snout of a tapir (Tapirus americanus).
claims.statement_id: Dalam Dicionário do Folclore Brasileiro, Cascudo menyebut Capelobo atau Cupelobo sebagai hewan fantastis berbadan manusia dengan moncong tapir (Tapirus americanus).
claims.quote: Capelobo. Cupelobo, animal fantástico, de corpo humano e focinho de anta (Tapirus americanus)

claims.statement: According to Cascudo, when it meets a large animal or a hunter, the Capelobo tears open its carotid and drinks the blood.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Cascudo, ketika bertemu hewan besar atau pemburu, Capelobo merobek arteri karotisnya dan meminum darahnya.
claims.quote: Encontrando bicho de porte ou caçador, rasga-lhe a carótida e bebe o sangue

claims.statement: Cascudo records that the Capelobo is said to be the werewolf (lobisomem) of the Indians.
claims.statement_id: Cascudo mencatat bahwa konon Capelobo adalah lobisomem (manusia serigala) orang Indian.
claims.quote: É o lobisomem dos índios, dizem.

claims.statement: According to Cascudo, the Capelobo gives itself away by its screams and has a foot shaped like the bottom of a bottle.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Cascudo, Capelobo mengungkap kehadirannya lewat teriakan dan berkaki berbentuk dasar botol.
claims.quote: Denuncia-se pelos gritos e tem o pé em forma de fundo de garrafa

claims.statement: Cascudo says the Capelobo resembles the Pé-de-Garrafa, with which it is partly confused.
claims.statement_id: Cascudo menyebut Capelobo mirip dengan Pé-de-Garrafa dan sebagian dikacaukan dengannya.
claims.quote: ao Pé-de-Garrafa, com o qual se confunde parcialmente

claims.statement: In a passage by S. Fróis Abreu quoted by Cascudo, the mysterious animal has a man's body covered in long hair and a head like that of the giant anteater (tamanduá-bandeira).
claims.statement_id: Dalam kutipan dari S. Fróis Abreu yang dimuat Cascudo, hewan misterius itu berbadan manusia berbulu panjang, dengan kepala seperti tamanduá-bandeira (trenggiling raksasa).
claims.quote: O misterioso animal tem corpo de homem, coberto de longos pêlos; a cabeça é igual à do tamanduá-bandeira

claims.statement: In the Fróis Abreu passage quoted by Cascudo, the animal sucks out the whole brain mass; the Indian said, "Supa o miolo" (it sucks the brain).
claims.statement_id: Dalam kutipan Fróis Abreu yang dimuat Cascudo, hewan itu menyedot seluruh isi otak; seorang Indian berkata, "Supa o miolo" (ia mengisap otak).
claims.quote: e sorve toda a massa cefálica: “Supa o miolo”, disse o índio.

claims.statement: Dzoavits was a demon or ogre of Shoshonean mythology who stole the sun and kidnapped children.
claims.statement_id: Dzoavits adalah iblis atau raksasa pemakan manusia dalam mitologi Shoshone yang mencuri matahari dan menculik anak-anak.
claims.quote: Dzoavits was a demon or ogre from Shoshonean mythology who stole the sun and kidnapped children.

claims.statement: He is associated with volcanism and cannibalism.
claims.statement_id: Ia dikaitkan dengan gunung berapi dan kanibalisme.
claims.quote: He is associated with volcanism and cannibalism.

claims.statement: In most legends he faces several mythological animals before being trapped in a cave, most commonly Devils Hole.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kebanyakan legenda, ia berhadapan dengan beberapa hewan mitologi sebelum terperangkap di sebuah gua, yang paling sering disebut Devils Hole.
claims.quote: In most legends he confronts several mythological animals before being trapped in a cave, the most common one being Devils Hole.

claims.statement: The Dzo'avits stories form a separate group of autochthonous tales; the Dzo'avits are described as a race of gigantic ogres dwelling in stone houses.
claims.statement_id: Cerita tentang Dzo'avits merupakan sekelompok kisah asli tersendiri; Dzo'avits digambarkan sebagai satu ras ogre raksasa yang tinggal di rumah batu.
claims.quote: those dealing with the Dzo'avits. These constitute a race of gigantic ogres dwelling in stone houses.

claims.statement: When a Dzo'avits slept, a Shoshone would sometimes creep up and shoot an arrow at his arms, but the arrow would break in two without disturbing him.
claims.statement_id: Ketika seorang Dzo'avits tidur, seorang Shoshone kadang merayap mendekat dan menembakkan panah ke lengannya, tetapi panah itu patah dua tanpa mengganggunya.
claims.quote: a Shoshone would sometimes creep up and shoot an arrow at his arms; but the arrow, instead of disturbing him, would break in two.

claims.statement: Individual members of this people are overcome by the Weasel brothers or, less often, by other Indians; the destruction of the whole tribe is ascribed to a conflagration caused by a number of birds or to the magic of Weasel-woman's uncle.
claims.statement_id: Anggota-anggota kaum ini dikalahkan oleh Weasel bersaudara atau, lebih jarang, oleh orang Indian lain; pemusnahan seluruh suku dikaitkan dengan kebakaran akibat sejumlah burung atau dengan sihir paman Weasel-woman.
claims.quote: Individual members of this people are overcome by the Weasel brothers, or, less frequently, by other Indians. The destruction of the whole tribe is ascribed to the conflagration caused by a number of birds, or to the magic of Weasel-woman's uncle.

claims.statement: The man in the moon is recognized as a giant cannibal (Dzo'avits), holding a blanket with one hand.
claims.statement_id: Manusia di bulan dikenali sebagai raksasa kanibal (Dzo'avits) yang memegang selimut dengan satu tangan.
claims.quote: The man in the moon is recognized as a giant cannibal (Dzo'avits), holding a blanket with one hand.

claims.statement: In the tale of the Weasels and the Giants, a Dzo'avits once caught Weasel's brother and devoured him.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah Weasel dan para raksasa, seorang Dzo'avits pernah menangkap saudara Weasel dan melahapnya.
claims.quote: Once a Dzo'avits caught Weasel's brother and devoured him.

claims.statement: In Powell's version, Dzo'avits is a witch ultimately transformed into the echo.
claims.statement_id: Dalam versi Powell, Dzo'avits adalah penyihir yang akhirnya berubah menjadi gema.
claims.quote: Powell, Dzo'avits is a witch ultimately transformed into the echo

claims.statement: Pa'-n-dzo'avits is a giant with enormous hands and feet who lives in the water.
claims.statement_id: Pa'-n-dzo'avits adalah raksasa bertangan dan berkaki sangat besar yang hidup di air.
claims.quote: Pa'-n-dzo'avits is a giant with enormous hands and feet, who lives in the water.

claims.statement: The Dorlis ("husband of the night") is a mythological creature in the culture of some African countries and the French West Indies (Martinique and Guadeloupe).
claims.statement_id: Dorlis ("suami malam") adalah makhluk mitologi dalam budaya beberapa negara Afrika dan Hindia Barat Prancis (Martinique dan Guadeloupe).
claims.quote: The Dorlis (or husband of the night) is a mythological creature that appears in the culture of certain African countries and in the French West Indies (Martinique and Guadeloupe).

claims.statement: It is an impure, invisible spirit that sexually harasses women (and sometimes men) at night, disturbing their rest.
claims.statement_id: Ia roh najis tak kasatmata yang melecehkan perempuan (kadang laki-laki) secara seksual pada malam hari dan mengganggu tidur mereka.
claims.quote: It is an impure and invisible spirit that sexually harasses women (and sometimes men) at night, physically overpowering them and disturbing their rest.

claims.statement: Its European equivalents are the incubus and succubus.
claims.statement_id: Padanannya dalam legenda Eropa adalah incubus dan succubus.
claims.quote: Its equivalent in European legends would be the incubus and succubus

claims.statement: In Martiniquan belief, the Dorlis can enter houses through cracks or keyholes by magic.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kepercayaan Martinique, Dorlis dapat masuk rumah lewat celah atau lubang kunci dengan cara gaib.
claims.quote: According to Martiniquan beliefs, the Dorlis can enter houses through cracks or keyholes using magical methods.

claims.statement: Its attack can be avoided by sleeping in black underwear or with nightclothes inside out.
claims.statement_id: Serangannya dapat dihindari dengan tidur memakai pakaian dalam hitam atau baju tidur terbalik.
claims.quote: methods exist to avoid its attack, such as sleeping in black underwear or with nightclothes worn inside out.

claims.statement: Another way is to put a container of salt by the bed, since the Dorlis must count every grain before acting.
claims.statement_id: Cara lain adalah menaruh wadah garam di dekat tempat tidur karena Dorlis harus menghitung setiap butirnya sebelum bertindak.
claims.quote: Another way to mislead the Dorlis is to place a container of salt near the bed, as the Dorlis would have to count every grain in it before it could act

claims.statement: The Dorlis is sometimes an excuse for illicit relationships, but can also manifest a psychological problem.
claims.statement_id: Dorlis kadang dijadikan dalih hubungan terlarang, tetapi juga bisa menjadi wujud masalah psikologis.
claims.quote: The Dorlis is sometimes used as an excuse for illicit relationships, but it can also be the manifestation of a psychological problem.

claims.statement: Writers use the Dorlis to reveal the fears and contradictions of French Antillean society.
claims.statement_id: Para penulis memakai sosok Dorlis untuk mengungkap ketakutan dan kontradiksi masyarakat Antilles Prancis.
claims.quote: The figure of the Dorlis is used by writers to reveal the fears and contradictions of French Antillean society.

claims.statement: Dimanche avec un Dorlis is a play by Patrick Chamoiseau, staged by Greg Germain.
claims.statement_id: Dimanche avec un Dorlis adalah drama karya Patrick Chamoiseau, dipentaskan oleh Greg Germain.
claims.quote: the play Dimanche avec un Dorlis (Sunday with a Dorlis), by Patrick Chamoiseau (staged by Greg Germain

claims.statement: According to this ethnopsychiatric study, in popular tradition the Dorlis is a figure who enters houses at night to sleep with women.
claims.statement_id: Menurut studi etnopsikiatri ini, dalam tradisi populer Dorlis adalah sosok yang menyelinap ke rumah pada malam hari untuk tidur dengan para perempuan.
claims.quote: Na tradição popular, o Dorlis é uma personagem que se introduz de noite nas casas, para dormir com as mulheres

claims.statement: According to the popular tradition recorded by the authors, the Dorlis is an ordinary man initiated by supernatural Powers, of normal appearance, who may practise a profession.
claims.statement_id: Menurut tradisi populer yang dicatat para penulis, Dorlis adalah pria biasa yang diinisiasi oleh Kekuatan supranatural, berpenampilan normal, dan dapat menjalankan suatu pekerjaan.
claims.quote: É um homem banal, iniciado por Potências sobrenaturais, com aparência normal e que pode exercer uma profissão

claims.statement: To enter, a keyhole is enough for the Dorlis, and he can also open doors with magic words. He is generally considered invisible and immaterial.
claims.statement_id: Untuk masuk, Dorlis cukup memakai lubang kunci, dan ia juga dapat membuka pintu dengan kata-kata gaib. Ia umumnya dianggap tak kasatmata dan tak berwujud.
claims.quote: Para entrar, basta-lhe um buraco de fechadura. Mas também sabe abrir as portas com a ajuda de palavras mágicas. Geralmente é considerado invisível e imaterial.

claims.statement: The Dorlis must always leave before the end of the night.
claims.statement_id: Dorlis harus selalu pergi sebelum malam berakhir.
claims.quote: O Dorlis deve sempre partir antes do fim da noite.

claims.statement: Before entering a house, the Dorlis smears himself with tallow or sulphur, which lets him escape if he is surprised.
claims.statement_id: Sebelum memasuki rumah, Dorlis melumuri dirinya dengan sebo (lemak) atau belerang, yang memungkinkannya meloloskan diri bila kepergok.
claims.quote: Antes de penetrar numa casa, o Dorlis besunta-se com sebo ou enxofre, o que lhe permite escapar se for surpreendido.

claims.statement: A village priest speaking in a personal capacity stresses the link between the Dorlis and the Devil; according to the authors, this association is rarely mentioned in Martiniquan popular tradition but is fairly widespread in Saint Lucia.
claims.statement_id: Seorang pastor desa yang berbicara atas nama pribadi menekankan kaitan antara Dorlis dan Iblis; menurut para penulis, kaitan ini jarang disebut dalam tradisi populer Martinique tetapi cukup tersebar di Santa Lucia.
claims.quote: O padre (que não pretende representar a opinião oficial da Igreja, e fala em nome pessoal) acentua a ligação existente entre o Dorlis e o Diabo. Esta associação, raramente evocada na tradição popular martinicana, está bastante difundida em Santa Lucia.

claims.statement: The authors found no belief strictly identical to the Dorlis outside Martinique.
claims.statement_id: Para penulis tidak menemukan kepercayaan yang benar-benar identik dengan Dorlis di luar Martinique.
claims.quote: Não encontrámos nenhuma crença estritamente idêntica a esta, fora da Martinica.

claims.statement: According to the French summary in the file, the incubi and succubi of Europe and the "Maji Nwé" of Saint Lucia are the closest relatives of the Dorlis.
claims.statement_id: Menurut ringkasan berbahasa Prancis dalam berkas itu, incubus dan succubus Eropa serta "Maji Nwé" dari Santa Lucia adalah kerabat terdekat Dorlis.
claims.quote: Les incubes et les succubes d’Europe et le «Maji Nwé» de Santa Lucia sont les parents les plus proches du Dorlis.

claims.statement: In the authors' psychoanalytic interpretation, the Dorlis acts as a valve that lets chimeras exist, authorizing the hallucinatory fulfilment of desire and channelling the return of the repressed.
claims.statement_id: Menurut penafsiran psikoanalitik para penulis, Dorlis berperan sebagai katup yang membiarkan khayalan ada, mengizinkan pemenuhan keinginan secara halusinatif, dan menyalurkan kembalinya yang tertekan.
claims.quote: o Dorlis tem assim o papel duma válvula, que deixa as quimeras existirem, autorizando a realização alucinatória do desejo, e canalizando o retorno do recalcado.

claims.statement: In the authors' view, the mechanism of belief in the Dorlis appears as a cultural ritualization of the erotic dream.
claims.statement_id: Para penulis, mekanisme kepercayaan pada Dorlis tampak sebagai ritualisasi budaya atas mimpi erotis.
claims.quote: O mecanismo da crença nos Dorlis, aparece como uma ritualização cultural do sonho erótico.

claims.statement: A theatre critic writes that in the pantheon of "magical" creatures from the Afro-Caribbean tradition, the Soucougnans and the Dorlis hold a privileged place.
claims.statement_id: Seorang kritikus teater menulis bahwa dalam panteon makhluk "gaib" dari tradisi Afro-Karibia, Soucougnan dan Dorlis menempati tempat istimewa.
claims.quote: dans le panthéon des créatures « magiques » issues de la tradition afro-caribéenne, les Soucougnans et les Dorlis, occupent une place privilégiés

claims.statement: In the play, the Dorlis materializes in a young woman's room, but trapped by daylight he cannot leave the room before nightfall because the sun would hurt him too much.
claims.statement_id: Dalam lakon itu, Dorlis menjelma di kamar seorang perempuan muda, tetapi terjebak cahaya siang ia tak bisa meninggalkan ruangan sebelum malam karena matahari akan terlalu menyakitkannya.
claims.quote: Joué par Gunther Germain, le malheureux Dorlis se matérialise dans la chambre de cette jeune femme, mais pris au piège de la lumière du jour, il ne peut plus quitter la pièce avant la tombée de la nuit car le soleil lui ferait trop mal.

claims.statement: Chamoiseau's play was created at the Chapelle du Verbe Incarné in 2004 and revived in Avignon with the same cast.
claims.statement_id: Lakon karya Chamoiseau ini pertama dipentaskan di Chapelle du Verbe Incarné pada 2004 dan dipentaskan lagi di Avignon dengan pemeran yang sama.
claims.quote: Créée à la Chapelle du verbe incarné en 2004 , la pièce de Chamoiseau est reprise cette année en Avignon avec la même distribution.

claims.statement: In Canadian folklore, Cressie is an eel-like lake monster said to live in Crescent Lake, Robert's Arm, Newfoundland and Labrador.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Kanada, Cressie adalah julukan monster danau mirip belut yang konon hidup di Crescent Lake, Robert's Arm, Newfoundland and Labrador.
claims.quote: In Canadian folklore, Cressie is the nickname given to an eel-like lake monster said to reside in Crescent Lake, Robert's Arm, Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada.

claims.statement: The name blends Crescent Lake and Nessie, the Loch Ness Monster's nickname.
claims.statement_id: Namanya gabungan dari Crescent Lake dan Nessie, julukan Loch Ness Monster.
claims.quote: The name is a portmanteau of Crescent Lake and Nessie, the nickname given to the Loch Ness Monster.

claims.statement: It has been described as a large dark brown eel about 15 feet long with a long, sleek body.
claims.statement_id: Monster ini digambarkan mirip belut besar cokelat tua sepanjang sekitar 15 kaki dengan tubuh panjang dan licin.
claims.quote: The monster has been described as resembling a large dark brown eel around 15 feet in length with a long, sleek body

claims.statement: Sightings of Cressie began in the 1950s and continue today.
claims.statement_id: Laporan penampakan Cressie dimulai pada tahun 1950-an dan berlanjut hingga kini.
claims.quote: Claims of Cressie being sighted began in the 1950s, and continue to the present day.

claims.statement: Some link it to earlier Indigenous legends of the woodum haoot ("pond devil") or haoot tuwedyee ("swimming demon").
claims.statement_id: Sebagian orang mengaitkannya dengan legenda pribumi woodum haoot ("iblis kolam") atau haoot tuwedyee ("iblis berenang").
claims.quote: some have linked the legends to earlier Indigenous legends of the woodum haoot ("pond devil") or haoot tuwedyee ("swimming demon")

claims.statement: Others caution that this link seems copied from source to source without verification.
claims.statement_id: Yang lain mengingatkan bahwa kaitan itu tampaknya disalin dari sumber ke sumber tanpa verifikasi.
claims.quote: others caution that this attribution has seemingly been copied from source to source without any verification

claims.statement: There are no photographs of Cressie; all information relies on local oral history.
claims.statement_id: Tidak ada foto Cressie; semua informasi bergantung pada sejarah lisan setempat.
claims.quote: There have been no photographs of Cressie, and all information relies on local oral history.

claims.statement: On July 9, 1991, Fred Parsons and his wife reported a large snakelike creature swimming in Crescent Lake.
claims.statement_id: Pada 9 Juli 1991, Fred Parsons dan istrinya melaporkan melihat makhluk besar mirip ular berenang di Crescent Lake.
claims.quote: On July 9, 1991, Fred Parsons and his wife reported seeing a large snakelike creature swimming in Crescent Lake.

claims.statement: Radford writes that Crescent Lake is a picturesque body of water in northeastern Newfoundland, Canada, near the small town of Robert's Arm.
claims.statement_id: Radford menulis bahwa Crescent Lake adalah perairan indah di timur laut Newfoundland, Kanada, dekat kota kecil Robert's Arm.
claims.quote: Crescent lake is a picturesque body of water in northeastern Newfoundland, Canada, near the small town of Robert’s Arm.

claims.statement: According to the information plaque quoted by Radford, local oral tradition traces sightings of Cressie to the turn of the century, when one of Robert's Arm's first residents, remembered as 'Grandmother Anthony', was startled from her berry picking by a giant serpent on the lake.
claims.statement_id: Menurut papan informasi yang dikutip Radford, dalam tradisi lisan setempat penampakan Cressie berawal dari pergantian abad, ketika salah satu penduduk pertama Robert's Arm, yang kini dikenang sebagai 'Grandmother Anthony', terkejut oleh seekor ular raksasa di danau saat memetik beri.
claims.quote: In the local oral tradition, sightings of Cressie go back to the turn of the century when one of Robert’s Arm’s first residents, remembered today as ‘Grandmother Anthony,’ was startled from her berry picking by a giant serpent out on the lake.

claims.statement: According to the plaque, in a daylight sighting of the early 1950s two local woodsmen saw what they thought was a boom log, which turned out to be huge, black and rounded and slipped beneath the lake.
claims.statement_id: Menurut papan informasi itu, pada sebuah penampakan siang hari awal 1950-an, dua penebang kayu setempat melihat sesuatu yang mereka kira batang kayu apung, yang ternyata besar, hitam, dan membulat lalu tenggelam ke dalam danau.
claims.quote: two local woodsmen on the shores of the lake noticed what they thought was a boom log just off shore. ... the men motored hurriedly out in time to witness the upturned ‘log,’ now huge, black, and rounded, slip beneath the waters of the lake.

claims.statement: According to the plaque quoted by Radford, on Thursday afternoon, September 5, 1991, at about 4:30 PM, Pierce Rideout, a resident of Robert's Arm, noticed a disturbance on the surface of Crescent Lake while driving his pickup truck.
claims.statement_id: Menurut papan informasi yang dikutip Radford, pada Kamis sore 5 September 1991 sekitar pukul 16.30, Pierce Rideout, warga Robert's Arm, melihat gangguan di permukaan Crescent Lake saat mengemudikan truknya.
claims.quote: On Thursday afternoon, September 5th, 1991, at approximately 4:30 PM, Mr. Pierce Rideout, a resident of Robert’s Arm, was driving his pickup truck at the approach to that town when he noticed a disturbance on the surface of Crescent Lake.

claims.statement: Radford quotes Fred Parsons saying he saw a long snake-like creature on the water, about fifteen or twenty feet long and dark brownish in colour.
claims.statement_id: Radford mengutip Fred Parsons: ia melihat makhluk panjang seperti ular di air, sepanjang sekitar lima belas atau dua puluh kaki dan berwarna cokelat gelap.
claims.quote: “What I saw was like a long, snake-like creature on the water,” he told me. “It was about fifteen or twenty feet long and a dark brownish colour

claims.statement: Radford writes that unlike the Loch Ness and Lake Champlain monsters, Cressie has never been photographed, and virtually all evidence for it comes from eyewitness sightings.
claims.statement_id: Radford menulis bahwa tidak seperti monster Loch Ness dan Danau Champlain, Cressie tidak pernah difoto, dan hampir semua bukti keberadaannya berasal dari kesaksian saksi mata.
claims.quote: Unlike the monsters in Loch Ness and Lake Champlain, Cressie has never been photographed; virtually all of the evidence for Cressie’s existence comes from eyewitness sightings.

claims.statement: According to Radford, virtually all witnesses agree that Cressie is dark and eel-like in appearance.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Radford, hampir semua saksi sepakat bahwa Cressie tampak gelap dan mirip belut.
claims.quote: One thing that virtually all witnesses agree on is that Cressie is dark and eel-like in appearance.

claims.statement: Radford concludes that the sightings are probably a mixture of misidentifications, floating logs, large fish, otters and perhaps even giant eels.
claims.statement_id: Radford berpendapat penampakan itu kemungkinan campuran salah identifikasi, gelondongan kayu terapung, ikan besar, berang-berang, dan mungkin belut raksasa.
claims.quote: The sightings are probably a mixture of misidentifications, floating logs, large fish, otters, and perhaps even giant eel.

claims.statement: Radford judges that the references to the woodum haoot and the haoot tuwedyee seem to have been copied from one source to another without verification of any actual connection to Cressie.
claims.statement_id: Radford menilai rujukan pada woodum haoot dan haoot tuwedyee tampaknya disalin dari satu sumber ke sumber lain tanpa diverifikasi memiliki kaitan dengan Cressie.
claims.quote: The references to the woodum haoot and the haoot tuwedyee seem to have been simply copied from one source to another without having been verified as having any actual connection to Cressie.

claims.statement: Radford writes that whether or not Cressie lurks in Crescent Lake, it certainly exists in the local folklore and imaginations.
claims.statement_id: Radford menulis bahwa terlepas dari ada tidaknya Cressie di Crescent Lake, ia pasti hidup dalam cerita rakyat dan imajinasi setempat.
claims.quote: Whether Cressie lurks in the waters of Crescent Lake or not, it certainly exists in the local folklore and imaginations.

claims.statement: Radford notes that the tourism effort began in the early 1990s when local resident Russell Bragg created the Cressie sign along the highway.
claims.statement_id: Radford mencatat bahwa upaya promosi wisata dimulai pada awal 1990-an ketika warga setempat Russell Bragg membuat papan Cressie di tepi jalan raya.
claims.quote: The main effort began in the early 1990s, when local resident Russell Bragg created the Cressie sign along the highway.

claims.statement: Radford mentions Cressie's Castle, a scenic area created especially for lake monster watching, reached by a twenty-minute walk along the lake.
claims.statement_id: Radford menyebut Cressie's Castle, area pemandangan yang dibuat khusus untuk mengamati monster danau, dapat dicapai dengan berjalan kaki dua puluh menit menyusuri danau.
claims.quote: a twenty-minute walk along the lake will bring you to Cressie’s Castle, a scenic area created especially for lake monster watching.

claims.statement: Crybaby Bridge refers to many bridges across the United States tied to urban legends and ghost stories of a baby crying.
claims.statement_id: Crybaby Bridge adalah sebutan bagi banyak jembatan di Amerika Serikat yang dikaitkan dengan legenda urban dan cerita hantu tentang suara tangis bayi.
claims.quote: Crybaby Bridge refers to numerous bridges across the United States, associated with urban legends and ghost stories involving the sounds of a baby crying.

claims.statement: These tales usually involve tragic backstories of infanticide, accidents or other sorrowful events near the bridges.
claims.statement_id: Kisah-kisah ini biasanya berlatar tragedi pembunuhan bayi, kecelakaan, atau peristiwa sedih lain di dekat jembatan.
claims.quote: These tales typically involve tragic backstories of infanticide, accidents, or other sorrowful events that purportedly occurred at or near the bridges

claims.statement: It is not tied to one place but is a type of folklore each region adapts to its own history and landscape.
claims.statement_id: Fenomena ini tidak terbatas pada satu tempat; ini jenis cerita rakyat yang disesuaikan tiap daerah dengan sejarah dan bentang alamnya.
claims.quote: The phenomenon is not limited to a specific location, but represents a type of folklore that has become embedded in the cultural fabric of various regions, each adapting the legend to fit local histories or landscapes.

claims.statement: A bridge on Sleepy Hollow Road between Jefferson and Oldham counties, Kentucky, was known as Crybaby Bridge.
claims.statement_id: Sebuah jembatan di Sleepy Hollow Road di perbatasan Jefferson dan Oldham, Kentucky, dikenal sebagai Crybaby Bridge.
claims.quote: A bridge on Sleepy Hollow Road near the border between Jefferson and Oldham counties in Kentucky was known as Crybaby Bridge.

claims.statement: In De Kalb, Texas, legend says a mother drove into the creek and the baby drowned in near-freezing water.
claims.statement_id: Di De Kalb, Texas, legenda menyebut seorang ibu yang mengemudi terjun ke sungai kecil dan bayinya tenggelam di air yang hampir beku.
claims.quote: Legend says that a mother driving a car plunged into the creek, and the baby drowned in the near-freezing waters.

claims.statement: According to an Ohio State University folklore project summary, Crybaby Bridges have many stories about how they became haunted, but all share an eerie cry said to be heard by those who follow the legend, which is thought to come from a ghost.
claims.statement_id: Menurut ringkasan proyek folklor Ohio State University, Crybaby Bridge punya banyak kisah tentang asal angkernya, tetapi semuanya sama dalam satu hal: tangisan seram yang konon terdengar oleh pengikut legenda dan diyakini berasal dari hantu.
claims.quote: Crybaby Bridges have many stories to how they have become haunted, but they all share one thing in common, an eerie cry is said to be heard by those that follow the legend, the cry is thought to come from a ghost.

claims.statement: The cry is often said to be either the baby's cry or that of the baby's mother.
claims.statement_id: Tangisan itu sering dikatakan sebagai tangis bayi atau tangis ibu si bayi.
claims.quote: The cry is often times said to be either a baby's cry or that of the baby's mother.

claims.statement: In the recording, Cory says what he has heard is that a mother threw her child off the train tracks onto the tunnel below, and that you are supposed to hear the babies cry if you stop in the middle of the bridge and turn your lights off.
claims.statement_id: Dalam rekaman itu, Cory mengatakan yang ia dengar ialah seorang ibu melempar anaknya dari rel kereta ke terowongan di bawah, dan tangis bayi konon terdengar jika orang berhenti di tengah jembatan dan mematikan lampu.
claims.quote: Cory said that what he has heard is that a mother threw her child off of the train tracks onto the tunnel below. He said that you are supposed to hear the babies cry if you stop in the middle of the bridge and turn your lights off.

claims.statement: There are many "Crybaby Bridges" in Ohio, and apparently one is located near Chillicothe.
claims.statement_id: Ada banyak "Crybaby Bridge" di Ohio, dan tampaknya satu di antaranya berada dekat Chillicothe.
claims.quote: There are many “Crybaby Bridges” in Ohio and apparently one is located near Chillicothe.

claims.statement: In an Indiana State University folklore archive account of a Crybaby Bridge in Morgan County near Martinsville, a woman's baby drowned while she was crossing a bridge, and visitors can now hear the baby crying and see her looking for the baby.
claims.statement_id: Dalam catatan arsip folklor Indiana State University tentang Crybaby Bridge di Morgan County dekat Martinsville, bayi seorang perempuan konon tenggelam saat ia menyeberangi jembatan, dan kini pengunjung dapat mendengar bayi menangis serta melihat sang ibu mencari bayinya.
claims.quote: This is Denise Rutledges typewritten account of the legend of Crybaby Bridge in Morgan County near Martinsville, collected by Sharon Fryar. According to legend, a womans baby drowned while she was crossing a bridge. Now if you visit the bridge you can hear the baby crying, and see her looking for baby.

claims.statement: In another variant in the same archive, for a Crybaby Bridge in Hamilton County near Carmel, Indiana, a family supposedly hanged one of its children on a bridge, and people travelling near it can hear a crying baby.
claims.statement_id: Dalam varian lain di arsip yang sama, untuk Crybaby Bridge di Hamilton County dekat Carmel, Indiana, sebuah keluarga konon menggantung salah satu anaknya di jembatan, dan orang yang lewat dekat jembatan itu dapat mendengar bayi menangis.
claims.quote: This is Brian Millers typewritten variant of the legend of Crybaby Bridge in Hamilton County near Carmel Indiana, collected by Granville Hayworth. According to legend a family hanged one of its children on a bridge. Now when travels near the bridge they can hear a crying baby.

claims.statement: In 1999, Maryland folklorist Jesse Glass argued that several crybaby bridges were not genuine folklore but fakelore knowingly propagated through the internet.
claims.statement_id: Pada 1999, folkloris Maryland Jesse Glass berargumen bahwa beberapa crybaby bridge bukan folklor asli melainkan "fakelore" yang sengaja disebarkan lewat internet.
claims.quote: In 1999, Maryland folklorist Jesse Glass presented a case against several crybaby bridges being genuine folklore, contending that they were instead fakelore that was knowingly being propagated through the internet.

claims.statement: In Kentucky, mothers reportedly dropped their unwanted, sick or deformed babies off the bridge to drown, and their crying can still be heard there.
claims.statement_id: Di Kentucky, konon para ibu menjatuhkan bayi yang tidak diinginkan, sakit, atau cacat dari jembatan hingga tenggelam, dan tangisan mereka masih terdengar di sana.
claims.quote: A bridge on Sleepy Hollow Road near the border between Jefferson and Oldham counties in Kentucky was known as Crybaby Bridge. Reportedly, mothers would drop their unwanted, sick, or deformed babies off the bridge to drown in the water, and their crying can still be heard there.

claims.statement: The Flathead Lake Monster is a lake monster of Indigenous legend and Montana folklore said to live in Flathead Lake, northwestern Montana, United States.
claims.statement_id: Flathead Lake Monster adalah monster danau dari legenda pribumi dan cerita rakyat Montana yang konon hidup di Flathead Lake, Montana barat laut, Amerika Serikat.
claims.quote: The Flathead Lake Monster is a lake monster of Indigenous legend and Montana folklore that is purported to dwell in Flathead Lake in northwestern Montana, United States.

claims.statement: The story originates in a Kutenai traditional legend.
claims.statement_id: Kisah monster di Flathead Lake berasal dari legenda tradisional Kutenai.
claims.quote: The story of a monster in Flathead Lake originates in a Kutenai traditional legend.

claims.statement: In the legend, the frozen lake split open and a monster's head with giant antlers rose through the ice.
claims.statement_id: Dalam legenda itu, permukaan danau yang beku terbelah dan kepala monster bertanduk rusa raksasa muncul dari balik es.
claims.quote: The frozen surface of the lake split open around them, and the head of a monster appeared through the ice, shaking its giant antlers.

claims.statement: Half the tribe drowned, said to be why there are so few Kutenai people.
claims.statement_id: Separuh suku tenggelam di danau, yang konon menjadi alasan jumlah orang Kutenai sedikit.
claims.quote: but half of the tribe drowned in the lake, which is said to be the reason why there are so few Kutenai people.

claims.statement: It was supposedly first reported in 1889 by Captain James C. Kerr of the steamboat U.S. Grant.
claims.statement_id: Monster ini konon pertama kali dilaporkan pada tahun 1889 oleh Kapten James C. Kerr dari kapal uap U.S. Grant.
claims.quote: It was supposedly first reported in 1889 by Captain James C. Kerr of the lake steamboat U.S. Grant.

claims.statement: According to Fugleberg, locals named it "Flessie", inspired by Loch Ness's "Nessie".
claims.statement_id: Menurut Fugleberg, warga setempat menamainya "Flessie", terilhami "Nessie" dari Loch Ness.
claims.quote: Fugleberg notes that local residents have named the purported lake monster "Flessie", inspired by Loch Ness' "Nessie".

claims.statement: It is usually described as a large eel-shaped creature with a wavy, snake-like body about twenty to forty feet long and brownish to bluish-black skin.
claims.statement_id: Ia biasanya digambarkan seperti belut besar bertubuh bergelombang seperti ular, panjang sekitar dua puluh hingga empat puluh kaki, berkulit cokelat hingga hitam kebiruan.
claims.quote: The monster is usually described as a large, round, eel-shaped creature with a wavy body like a snake about twenty to forty feet (6.1 to 12.2 m) long, having brownish to bluish-black skin and grayish-black eyes.

claims.statement: According to the Flathead Beacon, possibly the first modern account to gain credence came in 1889 from James Kerr, captain of the U.S. Grant, a steam-driven boat that ferried passengers and freight on the lake.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Flathead Beacon, kemungkinan catatan modern pertama yang dipercaya datang pada 1889 dari James Kerr, kapten U.S. Grant, kapal uap yang mengangkut penumpang dan barang di danau itu.
claims.quote: possibly the first modern account to gain credence came in 1889 from James Kerr, the captain of the U.S. Grant, a steam-driven boat that ferried passengers and freight up and down the lake.

claims.statement: Kerr reported seeing what he first thought was a large log; as the boat got closer, the "log", estimated at more than 20 feet long, began to move through the water.
claims.statement_id: Kerr melaporkan melihat sesuatu yang semula disangkanya kayu gelondongan besar; saat kapal mendekat, "kayu" itu, diperkirakan lebih dari 20 kaki panjangnya, mulai bergerak di air.
claims.quote: Kerr reported seeing what he initially thought was a large log. As the boat got closer, the “log,” estimated at more than 20 feet in length, began to move through the water.

claims.statement: In a quotation from a column carried by the Beacon, some sightings have been attributed to hyperactive imaginations, playful pranks, natural phenomena such as wave action, shadows and lighting effects, logs and a large number of animals.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kutipan dari sebuah kolom yang dimuat Beacon, sebagian penampakan dikaitkan dengan imajinasi berlebihan, kelakar, fenomena alam seperti ombak, bayangan, dan efek cahaya, kayu gelondongan, serta banyak hewan.
claims.quote: Some of the sightings have been attributed to hyperactive imaginations, playful pranks, natural phenomena such as wave action, shadows, lighting effects, logs and a large number of animals

claims.statement: In a quotation carried by the Beacon, most reports other than large-fish sightings describe it as long and eel-shaped, round, 30 to 40 feet in length, with large black eyes.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kutipan yang dimuat Beacon, kebanyakan laporan selain penampakan ikan besar menggambarkannya panjang dan seperti belut, bulat, sepanjang 30 sampai 40 kaki, bermata hitam besar.
claims.quote: Most, other than large fish sightings, describe it as long and eel-shaped, round, 30 to 40 feet in length with large black eyes

claims.statement: According to the Beacon, despite extensive netting, electro-shocking, small submarines and other research, no sign of sturgeon or other creatures has been found.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Beacon, meski ada penjaringan luas, penyetruman listrik, kapal selam kecil, dan penelitian lain, tidak ada tanda ikan sturgeon atau makhluk lain yang ditemukan.
claims.quote: Despite extensive netting, electro-shocking, small submarines that have ventured deep into the lake and other types of research, including time spent underwater in the forks of the Flathead River, no sign of sturgeon or other creatures has been found.

claims.statement: In 1955, C. Leslie Griffith caught a 7.5-foot, 181-pound white sturgeon near Dayton; it was displayed at the Polson museum and fuelled theories that sturgeon might be responsible for the sightings.
claims.statement_id: Pada 1955, C. Leslie Griffith menangkap sturgeon putih 7,5 kaki seberat 181 pon dekat Dayton; ikan itu dipajang di museum Polson dan memicu teori bahwa sturgeon menjadi penyebab penampakan.
claims.quote: In 1955, C. Leslie Griffith captured a 7.5-foot, 181-pound white sturgeon near Dayton. The massive fish was displayed at the Polson-Flathead Historical Museum and fueled theories that sturgeon — rare, deep-dwelling, and prehistoric-looking — might be responsible for the sightings.

claims.statement: According to oral history shared by Kootenai elders Catherine and Louise Andrew, a bird's wife used to feed huckleberries to a friendly lake creature; when her jealous husband found out, he killed the monster.
claims.statement_id: Menurut sejarah lisan dari tetua Kootenai Catherine dan Louise Andrew, istri seekor burung biasa memberi buah huckleberry kepada makhluk danau yang ramah; ketika suaminya yang cemburu mengetahuinya, ia membunuh monster itu.
claims.quote: According to oral history shared by Kootenai elders Catherine and Louise Andrew, a bird’s wife used to feed huckleberries to a friendly lake creature. But when the bird’s jealous husband discovered this, he killed the monster.

claims.statement: The creature's body became what is now called Sullivan Hill, near Elmo on the lake's western shore.
claims.statement_id: Tubuh makhluk itu menjadi bukit yang kini disebut Sullivan Hill, dekat Elmo di tepi barat danau.
claims.quote: The creature’s body became what is now called Sullivan Hill, near Elmo on the lake’s western shore.

claims.statement: In 2024, the city of Polson installed a 25-foot bronze statue of the creature in Sacajawea Park.
claims.statement_id: Pada 2024, kota Polson memasang patung perunggu setinggi 25 kaki makhluk itu di Sacajawea Park.
claims.quote: In 2024, the city of Polson installed a 25-foot bronze statue of the creature in Sacajawea Park

claims.statement: Some sightings identify it as a massive fish between 6 and 10 feet long, possibly a sturgeon.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian penampakan mengidentifikasinya sebagai ikan besar sepanjang 6 sampai 10 kaki, mungkin sturgeon.
claims.quote: Some sightings identify it as a massive fish between 6 and 10 feet in length — possibly a sturgeon.

claims.statement: The Flying Head (also Big Head or the Great Head) is a cannibalistic spirit of Haudenosaunee and Wyandot mythology.
claims.statement_id: Flying Head (juga Big Head atau Great Head) adalah roh kanibal dalam mitologi Haudenosaunee dan Wyandot.
claims.quote: The Flying Head (also known as Big Head or the Great Head) is a cannibalistic spirit from Haudenosaunee and Wyandot mythology.

claims.statement: Flying Heads are ravenous spirits cursed with insatiable hunger.
claims.statement_id: Flying Head digambarkan sebagai roh rakus yang dikutuk dengan kelaparan tak terpuaskan.
claims.quote: Flying Heads are described as being ravenous spirits that are cursed with an insatiable hunger.
